title: Grove deploys live capital through Instances whose RRC Framework implementation coverage is still marked Pending
content:
Each Instance Configuration Document opens with a field titled "RRC Framework Full Implementation Coverage." In this chunk it reads **`Pending`** for the Ripple RLUSD Instance (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.10.1.1), the Agora AUSD Instance (.11.1.1), and all three Uniswap v3 AUSD/USDC Instances (.12.1.1, .12.2.1, .12.3.1). It reads **`Covered`** only for Maple syrupUSDC (A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.3.1.13.1.1).

The surrounding text is unambiguous that these are not proposals. Each parent section states that the Instances "with `Active` Status are stored herein," and the Instances carry concrete pool addresses, live RateLimitIDs, and eight-figure deposit allowances.

The tension is therefore explicit on the face of the document: capital is allocated through five of six Instances before the risk framework's coverage of them is complete. The field's existence is a point in the Atlas's favour — the gap is disclosed in a structured, machine-readable slot rather than buried — but disclosure is not mitigation. A reader can enumerate exactly which live allocations are un-covered, and that enumeration is the finding.

It also gives the field a useful second life as a coverage backlog: the ratio of `Covered` to `Pending` across all Instances is a directly observable measure of how far Grove's actual book has run ahead of its formal risk process.
description: Ripple, Agora and all three Uniswap Instances read Pending while Maple syrupUSDC reads Covered, so active allocations run ahead of the risk framework meant to govern them.
